speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; how long has this been present, and can you describe the shape and depth of the ulcer?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

I have reviewed your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the ant bite report, but your ulcer is likely autoimmune rather than infectious. Given your risk factors for immunosuppression and the ulcerative nature, please proceed immediately with a biopsy of the lesion and a complete blood count (CBC) and C-reactive protein (CRP) to assess for neutrophilic dermatosis activity.
